ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Susan has two pendants made of the same material. They are equally thick and weigh the same. One of them has the shape of an annulus created from two concentric circles with the radii $6 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $4 \mathrm{~cm}$ (see the diagram). The second has the shape of a solid circle. What is the radius of the second pendant?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The accompanying diagram shows a gray shaded annulus, composed of two concentric circles; a horizontal line passes through the common center, the left side from the outer circle boundary to the center is labeled 6 cm, and the right side from the center to the inner circle boundary is labeled 4 cm. Therefore the outer circle radius is 6 cm, and the inner circle radius is 4 cm. Reasoning: The two pendants have the same material, the same thickness, and the same weight, so their volumes are the same; the thickness is also the same, therefore the front areas are the same. The annulus area is π(6^2 - 4^2) = π(36 - 16) = 20π. Let the radius of the second solid circular pendant be r, then its area is πr^2. Set πr^2 = 20π, obtaining r^2 = 20, so r = √20 = 2√5 cm.

raw_record.question_text: Susan has two pendants made of the same material. They are equally thick and weigh the same. One of them has the shape of an annulus created from two concentric circles with the radii $6 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $4 \mathrm{~cm}$ (see the diagram). The second has the shape of a solid circle. method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: it shows a shaded annulus formed by two concentric circles, with the outer radius labeled 6 cm and the inner radius labeled 4 cm along a horizontal radius line. From the text, use that the two pendants are made of the same material, have equal thickness, and weigh the same, so their face areas must be equal. Compute the annulus area directly as π(6^2−4^2)=20π. Let the radius of the solid circular pendant be r, so its area is πr^2. Equate πr^2=20π and solve r=√20=2√5 cm.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the pendant shown is a ring-shaped region, which can be viewed as a large circular disk of radius 6 cm with a concentric circular hole of radius 4 cm removed. From the text, since the two pendants have identical material and thickness and equal mass, compare the volumes or masses: density × thickness × face area is the same for both, so density and thickness cancel. Instead of invoking the annulus formula directly, compute the equivalent solid-circle radius x by subtracting disk areas: π·6^2−π·4^2=πx^2. Factor the difference of squares: x^2=36−16=(6−4)(6+4)=20, so x=2√5 cm.
